_README: Ongoing story threads for cross-day memory. The cloud agent appends/updates threads each run and prunes stale ones. Format per thread: {"id", "title", "first_seen", "last_update", "summary", "status"}.

threads.title: US-Israel war on Iran
threads.summary: Iran fired missiles at US forces in Jordan (intercepted); US and Saudi jets struck Iran-aligned targets in Iraq in response to prior drone attacks. The confrontation has since broadened into a declared U.S.-Israel war on Iran (launched February 2026): Tehran says the US will 'pay the price' for civilian deaths in a strike on Qeshm island, and NATO jets scrambled July 30 after a Russian missile detonated in Poland amid related regional tension. Aug 1: Trump says fresh US strikes on Iran are coming as soon as this weekend ('we'll be hitting them very hard'); Kuwait says it intercepted Iranian drones that struck a government facility and civilian vehicles, widening the conflict's geographic footprint. A new AP-NORC poll (July 23-27) puts Trump's overall approval at 33%, with about two-thirds of Americans saying the war has not been worth fighting. Aug 2: Trump reversed course, saying he is canceling the planned strikes because 'the perimeters of a deal' have been agreed to reopen the Strait of Hormuz and end Iran's nuclear program, after Saudi Arabia and other regional powers urged de-escalation; Iranian state media has given no indication Tehran requested the pause or agreed to any new terms, so the reported deal is unconfirmed from Iran's side. Aug 3: Trump says negotiations with Iran formally resume this afternoon; Iranian state media still has not confirmed requesting the pause or agreeing to any terms, so the deal remains unconfirmed from Tehran's side. Separately, Exxon and Chevron reported combined Q2 profits of $26.5B as Brent crude topped $112/barrel amid the conflict, drawing lawmaker criticism as a wartime windfall. Aug 4: Trump held off on renewed strikes, calling it a 'last chance' for Iran to sign a deal; a fourth cargo-ship attack hit a dry bulk vessel off Oman overnight (crew abandoned ship, one seafarer missing). Treasury Secretary Bessent said a Hormuz-reopening deal could land within a day, but Iran's foreign ministry denies any direct US talks are underway, saying it is only discussing a temporary safe shipping route with Oman. See separate thread for the Gaza/Hamas disarmament deal announced July 31, which runs alongside but is distinct from this war.

threads.title: Mass migrant crossing into Spain's Ceuta
threads.summary: Roughly 60,000 people crossed from Morocco into the Spanish enclave of Ceuta this week after a Spanish Supreme Court ruling made it harder to turn back migrants arriving by sea; social media posts encouraging the crossing are cited as a contributing factor. Outlets report death tolls ranging from at least 18 to over 60 (drownings and a stampede at a border fence), with most migrants having voluntarily returned to Morocco. Spain's PM is visiting the territory; France has tightened checks on its own border with Spain and Italy has floated suspending Spain from the EU's open-border scheme. Aug 1: Spain confirmed the death toll at 67 and said the situation has been 'almost entirely reversed,' with most migrants having voluntarily returned to Morocco; Spain is installing a 500-meter floating barrier along the border fence, and officials warned of possible additional uncounted casualties on the Moroccan side. Aug 2-3: Confirmed death toll has risen further to 72; roughly 22 EU heads of state have pointed to Spain's mass migrant regularization policy as a 'pull factor' behind the surge. Aug 4: Spain says about 69,500 migrants have now returned to Morocco over four days; Morocco's Interior Ministry blames the surge on social-media misinformation and trafficking networks, and Ceuta is now working through the aftermath (thousands still sheltering, some sleeping on sidewalks) rather than an active influx.

threads.title: Gaza ceasefire / Hamas disarmament deal
threads.summary: Trump announced Hamas agreed, via the Gaza Board of Peace, to a phased disarmament roadmap matched by Israeli withdrawal from Gaza; a detailed plan is due within 14 days. Neither Hamas nor Israel has publicly confirmed. Distinct from, but announced alongside, the ongoing wider US-Israel war on Iran. Aug 3 detail: the roadmap is expected to take 200-250 days, with Gaza police weapons transferred first to a new National Committee, followed by heavier weapons; Israel still hasn't publicly agreed, and Hamas says it won't proceed without a matching Israeli withdrawal. Aug 4: Israeli strikes killed dozens in Gaza over the weekend despite the deal announcement; Israel has conveyed 'serious concerns' about the roadmap to Washington and says it won't withdraw until Hamas is fully disarmed, citing intelligence that Hamas is still rearming and recruiting.

threads.title: Hyperscaler AI infrastructure buildout
threads.summary: Google raised 2026 capex guidance to $195-205B; Microsoft/3M, SoftBank France (5GW/E75B), and Chevron/Microsoft Texas power deal all point to accelerating AI data-center investment. Now confirmed: Nvidia is in talks for a ~$250B guarantee backing OpenAI's $500B, 10GW Ohio data-center lease (SoftBank's SB Energy), plus a separate ~$350B facility for OpenAI's chip purchases; analysts have begun calling the structure 'circular financing.' Same week, chip stocks (Nvidia, SK Hynix, Samsung, Micron, AMD, TSMC) shed over $1 trillion in combined market cap on doubts about AI capex sustainability. July 31: investor enthusiasm is concentrating on cloud-infrastructure hosts over model developers, and Microsoft is now positioning itself as a direct competitor to OpenAI/Anthropic (own models, agent tooling) rather than just their host; Q2 GDP data shows AI-related imports (chips, compute hardware) widening the US trade deficit and denting growth (1.5% vs 2.1% prior quarter). Aug 2: First hard demand-side confirmation — Amazon's Q2 earnings show AWS revenue up 37% YoY to $42.2B (vs. 31% expected), its fastest growth in 18 quarters, with AI/chip businesses each topping $25B annualized run rate; Amazon plans $220B in 2026 capex, suggesting the capex buildout still has enterprise demand behind it despite the chip-stock selloff. Aug 3: Global semiconductor industry revenue is projected to top $1 trillion in 2026 for the first time, led by AI-driven demand for computing/data-storage chips (>$500B, +41% YoY) — another demand-side data point alongside the capex/circular-financing debate. Aug 4: Palantir posted 93% YoY Q2 revenue growth ($1.94B) and 149% commercial-revenue growth, crediting demand for 'AI sovereignty' tools; shares jumped ~30% (best day ever) and helped push the S&P 500 toward a record — the first hard evidence this week that customer-facing AI product demand, not just hyperscaler infrastructure capex, is accelerating.

threads.title: Cisco SD-WAN active-exploitation campaign
threads.summary: State-aligned actor UAT-8616 has exploited seven Cisco SD-WAN zero-days in 2026 against government/critical-infrastructure targets; campaign remains active. No new disclosures as of July 30.

threads.title: France/Spain wildfires and heat wave
threads.summary: Wildfires have displaced roughly 330,000 people across France and Spain, the largest peacetime evacuation in French history; a new heat spike is forecast. No confirmed new figures as of July 30. Aug 2: Fires are stabilizing in both countries (Madrid-area and Gironde blazes both described as 'technically stabilized'); authorities have begun letting evacuees return home, though a fourth heat wave of the summer could still complicate the recovery.

threads.title: Japan (Kumamoto) earthquake recovery
threads.summary: Magnitude-7.1 quake near Kumamoto: death toll has climbed from 18 (July 29) to 34 as of July 31. Rescue operations continue at a collapsed shopping mall (Kashima) and a paper mill (Yatsushiro); over 10,000 remain in evacuation shelters, and extreme summer heat combined with water/power outages is raising heatstroke risk for displaced residents. Aug 4: One week on, the death toll holds at 38 (123 injured); response has shifted from search-and-rescue to survivor care, with record heat (40.3C on Aug 3) raising heatstroke risk for the ~9,200 people still in 210 shelters. Tokyo approved about ¥20 billion in reserve funds for relief and infrastructure repair, and the Self-Defense Force has airlifted air coolers to evacuation centers.

threads.title: Fauci Senate hearing / contempt-of-Congress threat
threads.summary: Fauci invoked the Fifth Amendment 100+ times in a Senate Judiciary hearing on COVID's origins. Committee chair Rand Paul plans a contempt-of-Congress vote next week; a referral would go to DOJ. July 31: public health experts now warn the spectacle could have a 'chilling effect,' discouraging future officials from serving in public health roles.

threads.title: Fed rate decisions
threads.summary: Fed held its benchmark rate at 3.5%-3.75% for a fifth straight meeting on July 29, with three FOMC members dissenting in favor of a hike. Stocks fell on the news; 30-year Treasury yield hit its highest level since 2007. July 31: Q2 GDP growth came in at 1.5% (down from 2.1%), with AI-driven imports widening the trade deficit; the 30-year mortgage rate hit 6.66% on July 30.

threads.title: Attacks on water-utility industrial controllers (PLCs)
threads.summary: Following attacks that disrupted 30+ community water systems in Minnesota and a separate incident in Michigan under FBI/possible-Iran investigation, CISA issued a July 30 alert warning that threat actors are targeting internet-exposed PLCs (Rockwell/Allen-Bradley, Siemens, Schneider Electric) at water and wastewater utilities in at least seven states, in some cases locking out operators. CISA is urging utilities to remove PLCs and other OT devices from direct internet exposure; cellular modems flagged as a common blind spot. Distinct from the ongoing Cisco SD-WAN campaign.

threads.title: INC ransomware exploitation of SonicWall SMA VPN flaws
threads.summary: Two SonicWall SMA 1000-series VPN appliance flaws (CVE-2026-15409/15410), chainable for arbitrary command execution, were patched in mid-July 2026. The INC ransomware group has since become the dominant exploiter of the pair, using a custom toolchain (KNUCKLEBALL loader, Suo5 proxy, ORANGETAIL web shell) and listing victims across the US, Australia and the UAE (private sector and government) as recently as August 2. Distinct from the ongoing Cisco SD-WAN and water-utility PLC campaigns.

threads.title: Michigan Democratic Senate primary
threads.summary: Michigan voters went to the polls Aug 4 in a closely watched Democratic Senate primary between Rep. Haley Stevens (establishment-backed) and physician/former state health official Abdul El-Sayed (running to her left), part of a 5-state primary day (Michigan, Missouri, Kansas, Virginia, Vermont) that has highlighted the party's divisions, including over Israel. Results were still coming in as of this digest.
